youtube_title: Lake Station, Indiana: Liverpool, the county seat Lake County lost (Lake Station request)
youtube:
You asked for Lake Station! Lake County once chose a county seat that vanished: Liverpool. It was laid out in 1836 where Deep River meets the Little Calumet, and in three days lots sold for $16,000. In 1839 it became the county seat and work began on a courthouse, but settlers protested, and in 1840 the seat moved to Lake Court House, soon renamed Crown Point. Historian T. H. Ball wrote that the unfinished courthouse was floated downriver on a scow to Blue Island, Illinois; others dispute that story. George Earle, who had pushed for Liverpool, went on to found Hobart, and in 1852 he laid out Lake Station. Liverpool emptied, and one historian wrote that fire took what was left. Its site lies in today's Lake Station and New Chicago, and no buildings remain. Comment your town, and it could be next! #LakeStation #NewChicago #LakeCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: John O. Bowers, 'Dream Cities of the Calumet' (Lake County Historical Association, 1929); T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900); both transcribed at inportercounty.org; Calumet Region Historical Guide (WPA, 1939); Lowell Public Library (Richard Schmal, Lowell Tribune); Crown Point Community Library; Lake County Historical Society; Town of New Chicago; Encyclopedia of Chicago. More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
